schema_version: v0 — skill-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: Interim checkpoint: stage, commit, and push the current work with a clear message. A non-terminal marker in the fluid middle, not a claim of doneness.
why: Work in the fluid middle needs recoverable checkpoints — a place to return to — that carry no false weight of completion. This is deliberately distinct from the durability-of-stones GATE (every stone committed + pushed), which belongs on the emit chokepoint as physics, not on a skill someone fires. A skill invented to force a behavior is policy standing in for a missing gate; keeping the two apart is what lets the checkpoint stay a light, honest act.
state: v0 — first cast 2026-07-15. The durability gate remains an IOU (CLAUDE.md 'rules awaiting physics').
distinction: interim-checkpoint SKILL vs durability-of-stones GATE — they coexist; collide only under an exclusive-and-terminal reading, which the learning-loop keystone forbids (see memory ask-the-why-to-distinguish).
how_it_learns: It doesn't, because mechanical: /commit is an interim checkpoint with no judgment to refine; the learning lives in the durability GATE it is distinct from, not here. A valid 'doesn't learn, because X' answer.
traces_to: Law 4 (durability is a gate awaiting physics, tracked as an IOU)
owner: the skills charter gates writes; Akien ratifies changes (signature gate)
guardrail: commit often and autonomously — mistakes are made in the COMMIT direction, so nothing important is left behind; end messages with the Co-Authored-By line; branch before committing durable work to a default branch.

counted_by.address_in_words: git log, commits carrying a Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer
counted_by.what_it_counts: commits CC authored. Measured 2026-08-04: 192. THIS IS A PROXY AND IT OVERCOUNTS — every /commit firing produces such a commit, but so does every commit CC makes without invoking the skill, which happens often. So the number is an UPPER BOUND on /commit firings, not the firings. It is carried anyway because an upper bound with its bias named is a measurement, and a dash is not.
counted_by.why_not_the_seam: git IS the trace. A commit is already a dated, authored, append-only record at a known address — wiring /commit to cairn.machines.skill_block would build a second ledger of the thing git exists to be. And this is the skill we most want frictionless: the two errors are asymmetric, an unnecessary commit costs a line of history and an uncommitted one can cost the work, so a door that adds a question here buys a number at the price of the behaviour.
counted_by.what_would_make_it_exact: a marker the skill writes and a bare commit does not — a trailer line, not a new store. Not built; the upper bound has been sufficient so far and building for it now would be building against no measured need.

proof: skill node → done only when cairnmap recompiles green (derivation gate). IOU until cairnmap exists — tracked in proofs/.
provenance: reclassified in the founding design conversation from 'a skill to force commits' to 'an interim-checkpoint utility'; the forcing role moved to a gate (MAP.md 'Gates, not supervisors', 2026-07-15). GUARDRAIL REVERSED 2026-07-29 (Akien, ratifying): 'commit/push only when Akien has asked' is retired — it was written for a condition no longer the case (Akien in the operator role, approving each outward act), and the founding intention is to get him OUT of that role. The asymmetry is the reason: an unnecessary commit costs a line of history, an uncommitted one can cost the work. Erring toward commit is therefore the honest default, not a liberty. Found from the far end: /saveslate wrote a slate over a dirty tree in both roots, so the continuity record was durable while the work it described was not.
